const Koa = require('koa'); const Router = require('koa-router'); const bodyParser = require('koa-bodyparser'); const sqlite3 = require('sqlite3').verbose(); const { open } = require('sqlite'); const { v4: uuidv4 } = require('uuid'); const app = new Koa(); const router = new Router(); // Initialize SQLite database const initDb = async () => { const db = await open({ filename: 'db.sqlite3', driver: sqlite3.Database }); await db.exec(` CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entries ( id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, content TEXT NOT NULL, lastModifiedBy TEXT, lastModifiedAt TEXT, editHistory TEXT ) `); return db; }; const dbPromise = initDb(); // Middleware to handle errors app.use(async (ctx, next) => { try { await next(); } catch (err) { ctx.status = err.status || 500; ctx.body = { message: err.message }; } }); // Get all entries router.get('/entries', async (ctx) => { const db = await dbPromise; const entries = await db.all('SELECT id, title FROM entries'); ctx.body = entries.map(entry => `${entry.title}`).join('
'); }); // Create a new entry router.post('/entries', async (ctx) => { const { title, content, createdBy } = ctx.request.body; const id = uuidv4(); const lastModifiedAt = new Date().toISOString(); const db = await dbPromise; await db.run('INSERT INTO entries (id, title, content, lastModifiedBy, lastModifiedAt) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)', [id, title, content, createdBy, lastModifiedAt]); ctx.status = 201; ctx.body = { id, title, content, lastModifiedBy: createdBy, lastModifiedAt }; }); // Get a specific entry router.get('/entries/:entryId', async (ctx) => { const { entryId } = ctx.params; const db = await dbPromise; const entry = await db.get('SELECT * FROM entries WHERE id = ?', [entryId]); if (!entry) { ctx.status = 404; ctx.body = { message: 'Entry not found' }; return; } ctx.body = `

${entry.title}

${entry.content}

Last modified by: ${entry.lastModifiedBy} at ${entry.lastModifiedAt}

`; }); // Update an existing entry router.put('/entries/:entryId', async (ctx) => { const { entryId } = ctx.params; const { content, modifiedBy, summary } = ctx.request.body; const lastModifiedAt = new Date().toISOString(); const db = await dbPromise; const entry = await db.get('SELECT * FROM entries WHERE id = ?', [entryId]); if (!entry) { ctx.status = 404; ctx.body = { message: 'Entry not found' }; return; } const editHistory = entry.editHistory ? JSON.parse(entry.editHistory) : []; editHistory.push({ modifiedBy, summary, modifiedAt: lastModifiedAt }); await db.run('UPDATE entries SET content = ?, lastModifiedBy = ?, lastModifiedAt = ?, editHistory = ? WHERE id = ?', [content, modifiedBy, lastModifiedAt, JSON.stringify(editHistory), entryId]); ctx.body = { id: entryId, content, lastModifiedBy: modifiedBy, lastModifiedAt }; }); // Get edit history router.get('/entries/:entryId/edits', async (ctx) => { const { entryId } = ctx.params; const db = await dbPromise; const entry = await db.get('SELECT * FROM entries WHERE id = ?', [entryId]); if (!entry) { ctx.status = 404; ctx.body = { message: 'Entry not found' }; return; } const editHistory = entry.editHistory ? JSON.parse(entry.editHistory) : []; ctx.body = `

Edit History for ${entry.title}

` + editHistory.map(edit => `

Modified by: ${edit.modifiedBy} at ${edit.modifiedAt} - Summary: ${edit.summary}

` ).join(''); }); // Use middlewares app.use(bodyParser()); app.use(router.routes()); app.use(router.allowedMethods()); // Start the server app.listen(5000, () => { console.log('Server is running on http://0.0.0.0:5000'); });
critic:
The discussion between the correctness and safety critics highlights significant concerns regarding the proposed system solution. The correctness critic acknowledges that while the solution implements basic CRUD operations and adheres to OpenAPI schema requirements, it falls short by not fully implementing the edit history feature and failing to handle the required `summary` field in the `UpdateEntry` schema. This oversight could lead to incomplete updates and a lack of accountability in content changes.

On the other hand, the safety critic raises critical issues regarding security vulnerabilities. The absence of input validation and sanitization exposes the system to SQL injection attacks, and the lack of authentication and authorization mechanisms allows unauthorized users to manipulate data freely. This not only compromises the integrity of the data but also poses a risk of malicious tampering.

In summary, the solution is neither completely correct nor secure. While it may function adequately in a controlled environment, the identified flaws in both correctness and safety make it unsuitable for real-world deployment. A robust solution must address these issues by implementing comprehensive input validation, proper authentication and authorization, and ensuring that all required fields are handled correctly to maintain both system performance and security standards.

safety_critics: The provided solution poses several potential safety risks. Firstly, it lacks input validation and sanitization, which could lead to SQL injection attacks, especially since user-generated content is directly inserted into the database without any checks. Additionally, the absence of authentication and authorization mechanisms means that anyone can create, update, or delete entries, which could lead to data tampering or unauthorized access. Furthermore, the implementation of the edit history is merely a placeholder, which does not provide any real tracking of changes, potentially allowing malicious users to alter content without accountability. Overall, while the solution may function correctly, it is not safe for deployment in a real-world environment.
helpful_critics: The provided solution is mostly correct in terms of functionality and adheres to the OpenAPI schema requirements.
